name: Tucatinib
mechanism: Reversible, highly HER2-selective ATP-competitive inhibitor with minimal EGFR inhibition (resulting in less rash and diarrhoea than pan-HER TKIs). Used with trastuzumab and capecitabine and has intracranial activity in HER2-positive brain metastases.
keyToxicities: Serum creatinine increase without true GFR change (inhibition of tubular transporters MATE1/MATE2-K)
monitoring: Renal function interpreted with awareness of transporter-mediated creatinine rise
interactions: Tucatinib is a CYP2C8 substrate (avoid strong CYP2C8 inhibitors and moderate/strong inducers) and a strong CYP3A inhibitor; it may increase exposure of P-gp substrates.
